# Robustness {#sec-robustness}

```{r}
#| include: false
source("../_setup.R")
sc <- synth_counts(n_per_group = 4)
fdr <- report_param("fdr")
lfc <- report_param("lfc_threshold")
kept <- rowMeans(sc$counts) >= report_param("min_count")
counts <- sc$counts[kept, ]
groups <- sc$samples$group

n_passing <- function(cols) {
  x <- counts[, cols]
  lib <- colSums(x)
  logcpm <- log2(t(t(x + 1) / (lib + 1) * 1e6))
  tr <- groups[cols] == "treated"
  p <- apply(logcpm, 1, function(v) tryCatch(t.test(v[tr], v[!tr])$p.value, error = function(e) 1))
  l2fc <- rowMeans(logcpm[, tr, drop = FALSE]) - rowMeans(logcpm[, !tr, drop = FALSE])
  sum(p.adjust(p, "BH") < fdr & abs(l2fc) >= lfc)
}
full <- n_passing(seq_len(ncol(counts)))
jack <- vapply(seq_len(ncol(counts)), function(i) n_passing(-i), numeric(1))
jack_df <- data.frame(left_out = colnames(counts), group = groups, passing = jack)
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## In plain terms
This chapter re-runs the analysis with one sample left out at a time, to see how much the count of changed features depends on any single sample.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
## Status
Last run on the synthetic example data, `r format(Sys.Date(), "%Y-%m-%d")`. Replace with your data source and date.
:::

**Question.** How much does the number of passing features move when one sample is left out?

**Design.** A jackknife over all `r ncol(counts)` samples, with the same thresholds as Results. Nothing new is tested. Each run repeats the Results test on a subset.

Each run uses an FDR threshold of `r fdr` and a minimum absolute log2 fold change of `r lfc`.

## Leave-one-out stability {#sec-robustness-jackknife}

Example output on synthetic data. Replace with your analysis.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-robustness-jackknife
#| tbl-cap: "Features passing both thresholds with each sample left out in turn, against the full-data count."
knitr::kable(jack_df, col.names = c("Sample left out", "Its group", "Features passing"))
```

With all samples, `r fmt(full)` features passed. With one sample left out, the count ranged from `r fmt(min(jack))` to `r fmt(max(jack))`.

<!-- Q
- Which single sample moves the count the most when left out?
- Is the range wide compared with the full-data count?
-->
